drivingQuestion: From whom do orphans collect only with an oath?
outcomeNote: Rav Yehuda's dictum is restated in the reverse form after Rava's difficulty

segments.he: מִמַּאן? אִילֵימָא מִלֹּוֶה — הַשְׁתָּא אֲבִיהֶן שָׁקֵיל בְּלָא שְׁבוּעָה, וְאִינְהוּ בִּשְׁבוּעָה?! אֶלָּא הָכִי קָאָמַר: וְכֵן הַיְּתוֹמִים מִן הַיְּתוֹמִים — לֹא יִפָּרְעוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבוּעָה.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «From whom» can the orphans collect payment only by means of an oath? «If we say» that they can collect payment only with an oath «from one who borrowed» money from their father, then it is difficult to understand how this can be so. «Now,» can it be that «their father,» the lender, had the right to «take» payment from the borrower «without an oath» by relying on the document, «and they,» the orphans, with regard to whom the Sages were lenient, can claim the loan only «by» means of «an oath? Rather, this is what» the mishna is «saying: And similarly, the orphans» of the lender who come to collect payment from «the orphans» of the borrower «can collect only by» means of «an oath.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַב זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאָמְרוּ יְתוֹמִים: אָמַר לָנוּ אַבָּא ״לָוִיתִי וּפָרַעְתִּי״, אֲבָל אָמְרוּ: אָמַר לָנוּ אַבָּא ״לֹא לָוִיתִי״ — אַף בִּשְׁבוּעָה לֹא יִפָּרְעוּ.
segments.en: «Rav Zerika said» that «Rav Yehuda said: It was taught» that those who take an oath can collect a debt from orphans «only if» the borrower’s «orphans said:» Our «father said to us: I borrowed and repaid. However,» if the orphans «said:» Our «father said to us: I did not borrow,» then «they may not collect» from the orphans «even» with «an oath.»

segments.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא, אַדְּרַבָּה: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר ״לֹא לָוִיתִי״ — כְּאוֹמֵר ״לֹא פָּרַעְתִּי״ דָּמֵי,
segments.en: «Rava objects to this: On the contrary,» there is a principle in the halakhot of claims that «anyone who says: I did not borrow is considered like one who says: I did not repay.» Therefore, when there is evidence that he did borrow, he must pay the entire amount without the lender having to take an oath.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אִי אִתְּמַר, הָכִי אִתְּמַר, אָמַר רַב זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאָמְרוּ יְתוֹמִים: אָמַר לָנוּ אַבָּא ״לָוִיתִי וּפָרַעְתִּי״, אֲבָל אָמְרוּ: אָמַר לָנוּ אַבָּא ״לֹא לָוִיתִי״ — נִפְרָעִין שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁבוּעָה. שֶׁכׇּל הָאוֹמֵר ״לֹא לָוִיתִי״ כְּאוֹמֵר ״לֹא פָּרַעְתִּי״ דָּמֵי.
segments.en: «Rather,» the Gemara emends the above statement: «If it was stated, it was stated like this: Rav Zerika said» that «Rav Yehuda said: They taught» this halakha «only if the orphans said:» Our «father said to us: I borrowed and repaid. However,» if «they said:» Our «father said to us: I did not borrow,» those who collect debts from them «can collect» even «without an oath, for anyone who says: I did not borrow is considered like one who says: I did not repay.»
